transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Ignition Grid - Head of Platform), Jin Park (Ignition Grid - SRE), Ava Martinez (Ignition Grid - BDR)

Auto-summary (generated):
- Intro / partner fit discussion for GPU + edge routing integration between Redwood and Ignition Grid.
- Ignition wants predictable cost for bursty inference and private VPC option; evaluating host vs dedicated vs on-prem.
- Agreed to run a small benchmark pilot; Redwood to provide perf harness and initial pricing bands.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and pain points (cost unpredictability, cold-starts, KV-caching)
- Deployment modes: Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) and hybrid routing
- Performance expectations: p50/p95 latency, throughput, batching strategies
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM, outbound IPs, audit logs
- Pilot framing + next steps

Transcript body (timestamps roughly every ~30s, transcription contains artifacts and occasional mislabels):
[00:00] Ethan: Hey thanks everyone for joining, I'm Ethan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this relationship, with me is Priya our SE.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, quick wave. we'll talk tech and then figure out a pilot, thanks for carving time.
[00:20] Liam: Hey thanks, Liam here. Quick context, Ignition Grid is a telco-edge provider and we're trying to standardize inference across our edge POps and cloud backends. We're looking at both cost and SLA.
[00:34] Ava: and I'm Ava, I'm mostly coordinating vendor evals and commercial stuff, happy to help with scheduling.
[00:40] Jin: Jin here, I'll own the SRE side, network, infra, and we'll run the bench.
[00:48] Ethan: Awesome. can you tell us about the current stack? what are you running now, clouds, on prem, GPUs?
[00:57] Liam: Yeah so main workloads are in multi-cloud, we have long tail on AWS regions and a private colo for latency-sensitive nodes. Mostly NVIDIA A10s and a few A100s, some custom Arm hosts for model shards. We kind of cobbled together an internal serving layer but it's getting expensive and brittle, so evaluation for external inference infra.
[01:21] Priya: Got it. when you say "brittle" can you give an example? cold-starts, queuing, memory pressure?
[01:28] Liam: All of the above, but especially cold KV cache misses when a model is warm in one region but cold in another. Also cost spikes when batch sizes change.
[01:36] Jin: And we don't have good tracing per-token cost, so ops can't easily identify when a particular route or prompt is burning money.
[01:45] Priya: That's exactly where Redwood's routing and prefix-KV-caching helps, we do automatic prefix cache and can route by latency or cost policy. Sounded like you'd benefit from caching + burst capacity.
[01:58] Jin: How mature is the KV cache? is it sticky across replicas, or is it per instance?
[02:05] Priya: It's per tenant with shared cache semantics — um the runtime materializes a KV store per model version and does LRU eviction, sticky across a pool. sometimes the transcription here will say K V cache, or K-V cache, apologies for noise.
[02:22] Liam: Ok that helps. what are the deployment options if we want to keep control of networking? we need VPC and egress control.
[02:30] Ethan: We support three modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployment (VPC / on-prem). For regulated routes you can bring Redwood Private into your VPC with customer-managed networking and you control egress IPs.
[02:45] Ava: do you have references for customers doing similar colo/edge onramps?
[02:49] Ethan: Yes, I'll share a short partner case study and an integration checklist.
[02:54] Jin: great. on security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for key management, and detailed audit logs. can you cover those?
[03:03] Priya: Yes SOC 2 attestation is available, we integrate with KMS/HSM providers for envelope encryption, and we surface audit logs via the console and syslog / S3 export. We'll drop links in the follow-up.
[03:16] Liam: cool. price sensitivity — we want to understand per-token pricing vs committed reserved pools. also if quantization or int8 options change pricing.
[03:27] Ethan: Two levers — hosted per-token for bursty usage, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput (monthly commits), and Private pricing which is license + infra. Optimize uses recommendations for quantization and batching that lower cost per token depending on model and workload. We'll send pricing bands.
[03:44] Jin: Do you support model variants for fallback? say p95 SLO missed, fallback to smaller model?
[03:50] Priya: Yes, our smart routing supports policies to fallback to compatible model variants or different regions and even throttle. You can define canary rollouts and automatic fallback rules in the console.
[03:59] Liam: On network topology — we have NAT gateways, egress IP pools and strict firewalling in colo, so if Redwood Private is deployed in our VPC, what's the outbound pattern?
[04:12] Priya: For Private you run the control-plane with Redwood but data path stays in your VPC. We publish the minimal outbound endpoints for control plane; for hosted you'd need allowlist IPs. We'll provide a network diagram.
[04:25] Jin: we'll need exact ports and IP ranges for firewalling.
[04:29] Ethan: we'll include that in the tech deep dive materials.
[04:32] Ava: timeline wise, if we wanted a pilot, what's realistic? 3–4 weeks?
[04:37] Priya: A minimal pilot can be 2–3 weeks if you provide model artifacts and sample traffic; 4 weeks is safer to validate regressions and SLOs.
[04:46] Liam: What would you need from our side to start?
[04:49] Priya: Representative model or a small set of prompts, expected qps distribution, target p50/p95 latencies, and a test harness to replay traffic. We'll also want the network topology and security contacts.
[05:01] Liam: We can provide a 10K qps day sample and a batch of convo prompts. We'll also include a heavier tail scenario.
[05:09] Ethan: Perfect. on the topic of hardware — you mentioned A10 and A100s. Redwood picks kernels and quantization paths depending on hardware. For A10s we might recommend certain batch sizes and int8 quantization to get cost parity with A100 int4 in some cases, we can show data.
[05:27] Jin: Are you doing compilation per model or per architecture? like custom kernels?
[05:31] Priya: The runtime auto-selects kernels based on model arch, sequence-length distribution and hardware; we also support model-specific compilation to optimize attention kernels. There's some hand tuning for new models but most common ones are optimized already.
[05:44] Liam: Any limiter on model size? We have a couple 30B models.
[05:48] Priya: We serve up to 70B with sharding; but memory/split math changes based on quantization and kv cache footprint. We'll outline memory footprint estimates.
[05:58] Ava: Who usually owns the integration on Redwood side during pilot? single point?
[06:03] Ethan: AE + SE pair — I'll be primary commercial, Priya on technical. For Private or Dedicated you'll get a solutions engineer and assigned CSM if you convert to reserved.
[06:12] Jin: For perf tests, do you have a standard harness we can use or do you want a bespoke script?
[06:17] Priya: We have a perf harness (python + golang clients) that replays traffic, supports KV warming and collects token-level traces and cost. I'll share it.
[06:25] Liam: Great. Can we test both hosted and private? We'd like a baseline on hosted then run private to see network delta.
[06:32] Priya: Yes recommended path is hosted baseline for speed then Private for final SLO parity.
[06:38] Ethan: Pricing differential will vary — hosted per token vs private license + infra. We'll provide an apples-to-apples cost model.
[06:45] Jin: Are there any known gotchas for on-prem GPUs with your runtime? e.g., CUDA driver versions or container images?
[06:52] Priya: We publish supported drivers and container images. Biggest issues historically are mismatched CUDA/cudnn versions and old NCCL setups; we have a checklist. Also certain perf taps require kernel drivers on specific enterprise distros.
[07:05] Liam: Ok. for compliance if we run Private on our VPC, can you still give us audit logs for requests and token usage?
[07:12] Ethan: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM, and we support syslog/OTel hooks.
[07:18] Ava: Any reference on uptime SLA for Dedicated pools?
[07:22] Ethan: Our Dedicated offering carries an SLA with uptime and latency SLOs tied to reserved capacity commitments — we'll share the terms doc.
[07:30] Jin: How does autoscaling work with reserved capacity? we have burst patterns, night spikes.
[07:36] Priya: You can configure burst capacity and autoscaling policies. For reserved pools we guarantee baseline throughput; bursts can consume on-demand capacity or fall back to hosted routing depending on policy.
[07:49] Liam: Are there cost controls per-route? We want dev vs prod segregation and budgets.
[07:53] Priya: Console supports per-route quotas, tokens caps, and billing tags. We can emit alerts on threshold.
[07:59] Ava: On the partnership front, we'd also want co-marketing and a partner onboarding packet.
[08:04] Ethan: We'll include partner packet and a short co-sell outline.
[08:08] Jin: one more technical — how do you handle KV cache warmup across multiple edge locations? does Redwood do global prewarming?
[08:17] Priya: There's a cache prewarm option where you can seed frequent prefixes; otherwise cache warms organically, but we have heuristics to prefetch based on traffic patterns. For edge fabric we colocate cache pools to reduce cross-region pulls.
[08:32] Liam: Sounds promising. let's talk pilot goals: we'd like p95 < 120ms for small chat models and cost per 1K tokens to be under X (we'll provide target X).
[08:44] Priya: Noted, we'll run baseline and see. we'll include recommendations — int8 quantization and small sequence-length micro batching usually lowers p95.
[08:53] Ethan: Ok let's talk logistics: I'll share deck, pricing bands, SOC2 link, case study. Priya will share perf harness and a concrete pilot plan with metrics. Liam you'll share model artifacts and expected qps. Jin will hand off network diagram. Ava coordinate scheduling.
[09:07] Ava: Works for me.
[09:10] Liam: Good. Any blockers on your side?
[09:13] Priya: Nothing immediate, maybe clarify which models to test.
[09:17] Liam: We'll pick one 7B and one 30B to cover small and medium-large.
[09:21] Ethan: Perfect. we'll sketch a 3-week pilot that starts with hosted baseline week 1, private deployment week 2, tuning week 3, deliverable is a perf report + recommend route to production.
[09:33] Jin: timeline sounds good.
[09:35] Ethan: ok last few quick Qs — who else on your side needs to be in the technical deep dive?
[09:41] Liam: We'll include netops and security (I'll invite our InfoSec lead).
[09:45] Ava: I'll coordinate the calendar invites.
[09:48] Ethan: Thanks everyone. we'll send notes and next steps.
[09:52] [END]
file_notes: Call included AE+SE pairing; medium transcription quality with some acronyms split. Customer is 'Ignition Grid' — edge/telco workload, interested in private/VPC and hybrid host/dedicated. Unique doc vs existing files.
